newsitem.title: THAILAND: Enhanced economic team seen after Thai polls.
newsitem.headline: Enhanced economic team seen after Thai polls.

text.p: Thailand's slowing economy received a psychological boost from expectations that it would be steered by a respected economic team after the November 17 general elections, analysts said on Sunday.
Analysts said the Democrat Party, expected to emerge as the biggest bloc in parliament, would likely lead a new coalition that would inspire qualified economists and bankers to join the government.

"The Democrats have the best chance of coming out on top," said Suchit Bungbongkarn, political lecturer at Chulalongkorn University, adding that this might encourage politicians from other parties to switch sides and run under the party's banner.

Analysts expect the Democrat Party, led by former Premier Chuan Leekpai, to improve on its performance in the last elections in July 1995 when it captured 86 of 391 seats of the House of Representatives, trailing the Chart Thai Party of outgoing Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa.
Banharn, who dissolved his six-party coalition on Friday after his partners tried to force him to step down, faces a major split in his 91-seat party.

Chart Thai's secretary general Sanoh Thienthong announced on Saturday he would spearhead a move to oust Banharn from the party leadership. The politician heads a Chart Thai faction that controls about 10 members of parliament.
Analysts said Chart Thai, facing mass defections by member MPs, could see the number of its parliamentary seats halved after the poll. It currently holds 91 seats.
Suchit and other analysts said the Thai stock market had been a victim of the crisis of confidence faced by Banharn's coalition. Thai stocks fell to near three-year lows earlier this month.
During a no-confidence debate against Banharn this month, the opposition accused him of economic mismanagement and of condoning corruption. Banharn denied the charges.
"Our economic problems this year stem from a public distrust in government integrity. With that feeling removed, I think we will see a better trend in the medium and long term," Suchit said.

Analysts said the market would welcome a Democrat-led coalition that put former Finance Minister Tarrin Nimmanahaeminda and Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs Supachai Panichapakdi back in the jobs they held during 1993-1995.

Songglod Bhichaikul of United Securities Plc expected Thai stocks to stage sharp rallies this week but said investors would be sidelined, after the initial euphoria, by weak third-quarter corporate earnings and poor economic fundamentals.

Thai exports rose only 2.9 percent during January/July against 26.5 percent a year ago. Gross domestic product is projected by private economists to grow at a 10-year low of seven percent this year against 8.6 percent in 1995.
